channel.title: Writing · Rory McClelland
channel.description: Notes on building with AI, privacy and safety, and bringing AI into organisations.

item.title: Keep your voice on your own machine
item.description: I have swapped a cloud dictation app for OpenWhispr, which transcribes speech on the local PC. It is a touch slower, it costs nothing, and my voice stays with me.

item.title: What your open tabs say about you
item.description: A small Firefox add-on sorts my tabs into groups with AI. The model runs on the local PC, so one of the most revealing lists on my computer never leaves it.

item.title: Attack it before anyone else does
item.description: Every system I build goes through a red team before I trust it: a deliberate attempt to make it fail. The bugs it finds matter more than the pass mark.

item.title: The approximation tax
item.description: AI makes it cheap to build exactly the software you need. That changes what people are willing to pay for the rest.

item.title: Private from whom?
item.description: Why "I want privacy" is not yet a requirement, and the two questions that turn it into one.

item.title: Write the never list first
item.description: Before deciding what an AI system should do, I write down what it must never do. Then each line is made true in code.

item.title: The method should outlast the consultant
item.description: The most valuable thing an AI programme can leave behind is a way of thinking the organisation can run for itself.
